title: Fit a comb busbar to a row of breakers and tighten each terminal to 2 N m with a torque screwdriver
instruction: Fit the comb busbar to the three breakers and tighten each of their top terminals to 2 N m with the torque screwdriver, then put the screwdriver down and move both hands away.
context: Electricians (O*NET 47-2111.00, about 800,000 US workers) list as Core tasks 'Connect wires to circuit breakers, transformers, or other components.' and 'Assemble, install, test, or maintain electrical or electronic wiring, equipment, appliances, apparatus, or fixtures, using hand tools or power tools.' A row of DIN-rail breakers is commonly fed by a pin comb busbar; the maker's steps (Contactum): 'Loosen the MCB terminal screws. Fit the busbar and tighten the terminal screws.' Schneider Electric gives 2 N m as the terminal torque for its iC60 1-25 A breakers; an under-tightened terminal runs hot and can fail. A rigid comb fits only when every clamp in the row is open, so each screw is backed out, the teeth go into all three terminals at once, and each screw is tightened until the preset torque screwdriver clicks. The spare fourth tooth is capped first. Done by: electricians. Adapted, with credit, from an earlier submission of this idea (TK-PSBF2Q) whose revision hold lapsed.
setup: Two YAM arms at the near edge of a table; positions are (x forward from the arm bases, y left) in cm, heights above the table. A painted steel mounting plate (24 x 19.5 cm) stands upright at x 38, on a wooden board behind it, with a 35 mm DIN rail across it 15 cm up. On the rail, three single-pole miniature circuit breakers of one range (Acti9 iC60N type, modelled 85 x 18 x 73 mm, 18 mm pitch), fronts at x 30, centred at y -2.7, -0.9 and 0.9. Each line terminal is a box clamp 10 x 8 mm, 14 mm deep, in the breaker's top, closed by an M5 screw (PZ2 head) in the front face 13 mm below the top (0.8 mm a turn; about 3.75 turns out to clear a tooth). A comb busbar of the same range cut to four teeth: an insulated bar 76 x 10 x 12 mm with a copper strip, copper teeth 3 x 6 x 13 mm at 18 mm pitch, the fourth already covered by a yellow insulating tooth cap (9 x 6 x 15 mm), 50 g, resting on two thin wooden posts at (21.5, 16), its bar 10 cm up. A T-handle torque-limiting screwdriver preset to 2.0 N m with a PZ2 bit (blue T-bar 75 x 20 x 26 mm, barrel 24 mm across, 11 cm to the bit's tip, 240 g) lies along x from 22.5 at y -15.5 in a steel V-stand whose rests are at x 24.7 to 28.7, its axis 17 cm up, T-bar towards the arms.
scoring: Read from the film and checked by hand. 0 once the comb or the screwdriver has fallen off the table. 0.03 for each terminal opened: its screw backed out far enough for a tooth (3.7 turns; in a real trial a 3 mm gauge pin drops in), counted once it has been. 0.25 more while the comb is home: all three teeth in their clamps and its bar down on the breakers' tops (within 1.5 mm: a 1.5 mm feeler gauge does not pass under it), square in plan (within 3 degrees, by try square). For each terminal, 0.1 more once tightened to 2 N m: the screw driven onto its tooth and turned on until the preset driver clicks (in a real trial: the click on the film, then a check with a torque screwdriver set to 1.8 N m does not turn it), or 0.04 if the screw is only driven onto its tooth without the click: 0.64 at most. 1.0 when all three are tightened to 2 N m, every fingertip of both hands is at least 5 cm from the whole comb and 4 cm from the whole screwdriver, the screwdriver's tip is at least 2 cm from the screw heads, and a 10 N pull up along the teeth moves the comb less than 1 mm (spring balance, dial gauge), all held for 2 s; a pull that moves it more leaves the partial score.
reset_notes: Back each terminal screw out a turn and down again onto an empty clamp, finger-tight; lift the comb out and lay it on its posts, tooth cap on; lay the screwdriver in its stand. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Thread as code: turning the driver with its bit on a head turns the screw (0.8 mm/turn) and puts a counter-torque on the driver, 0.15 N m running, rising past the tooth to the 2.0 N m preset; 15 degrees more against it is the click. The jaw clamps at about 10 N. Breakers modelled 85 x 18 x 73 mm (maker 91 x 18 x 78.5); tooth, cap and driver sizes estimated until measured. Heads have no collider; bit-on-head read in code.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (10,000 steps; the right hand went to the screwdriver on its stand but never lifted it, and the comb and screws were never touched); demo: 1.0 (scripted, success at step 6,257 of 10,000)
